Let the non-base vertices be ordered as
\[
a_1,a_2,a_3,b_1,b_2,b_3,
\]
and put
\[
K_{ij}(p,s)=\frac{d_s(i,\ast)^p+d_s(j,\ast)^p-d_s(i,j)^p}{2}.
\]
For coefficients with total sum \(0\), writing the six non-base coefficients as \(x\), one has
\[
\sum_{z,w}c_zc_wd_s(z,w)^p=-2x^TK(p,s)x.
\]
Thus \(p\)-negative type is equivalent to \(K(p,s)\succeq0\).

For small \(s>0\), the only distances changed from the two unchorded \(4\)-cycles are
\[
d(a_1,a_3)=2-4Ls+s^2,\quad d(b_1,b_3)=2-4Ls,\quad
d(a_2,b_2)=4-(8L-12M)s.
\]

At \(s=0,p=1\), the kernel of \(K\) is spanned by
\[
u=(1,-1,1,0,0,0),\qquad v=(0,0,0,1,-1,1).
\]
For \(p>1\),
\[
u^TK(p,0)u=4-2\cdot 2^p<0,
\]
so \(\wp(0)=1\).

Now write
\[
p=1+qs+rs^2+O(s^3).
\]
Taking the Schur complement against the four positive directions at \((p,s)=(1,0)\), the active \(2\times2\) block on \(\operatorname{span}\{u,v\}\) has expansion
\[
S=s(1-q)H+s^2(G-rH)+O(s^3),
\]
where
\[
H=\begin{pmatrix}
4L&4L-6M\\
4L-6M&4L
\end{pmatrix}
\]
is positive definite, and
\[
G=\begin{pmatrix}
g_1&g_3\\
g_3&g_2
\end{pmatrix},
\]
with
\[
g_1=4L+2L^2-1-\frac92(L-M)^2,
\]
\[
g_2=4L+2L^2-\frac92(L-M)^2,
\]
\[
g_3=4L^2-6LM+3M^2+4L-6M.
\]
Since \(H\succ0\), the linear term forces \(q=1\). The first loss of positive semidefiniteness at the next order occurs when
\[
\det(G-rH)=0,
\]
taking the smaller root. Thus
\[
r=\frac{4L(g_1+g_2)-2(4L-6M)g_3-\sqrt{\left(4L(g_1+g_2)-2(4L-6M)g_3\right)^2-4\left((4L)^2-(4L-6M)^2\right)(g_1g_2-g_3^2)}}{2\left((4L)^2-(4L-6M)^2\right)}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\wp(s)=1+s+rs^2+O(s^3),
\]
so
\[
\boxed{\left(1,\ 1,\ 2r\right)}.
\]

Numerically,
\[
2r\approx 1.36026934240001.
\]
